details.summary: This is an excellent, highly practical lunch recipe that perfectly hits the target macronutrient windows, uses everyday ingredients, and genuinely requires less than 30 minutes. The only necessary fix is adding a 'check at 10 minutes' phrase to the pasta cooking step to fully align with the instruction guidelines.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is well-balanced. Peanut butter, lime, soy sauce, garlic, and red pepper flakes create a classic, savory, tangy, and slightly spicy dressing that pairs excellently with the vegetables and chicken.
All listed ingredients are used in the instructions exactly as stated, and the addition of 1 tablespoon warm water to the dressing is an appropriate and well-handled instruction.

The pasta cooking time provides a range ('10 to 12 minutes') and a doneness cue ('until tender'), but it lacks an explicit check instruction at the minimum time. Change Step 2 to: 'Add the spaghetti and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, checking at 10 minutes to see if it is tender.'
The ingredients and techniques align perfectly with an Asian-American peanut noodle salad.
Boiling the pasta and using a no-cook dressing method is perfectly suited for this quick, cold lunch salad.
The computed nutrition values align closely with the ingredients (100g whole wheat pasta, 170g chicken breast, vegetables, and 1.5 tbsp peanut butter).
The title accurately reflects the dish, and the intro uses a practical, pragmatic tone that matches the book's character without making banned health claims.
This is a highly appealing, quick, and satisfying lunch that offers great contrasting textures (crisp cabbage, chewy noodles) and a creamy sauce.

The dish serves both conditions beautifully: it relies on lean protein, healthy unsaturated fats (peanut butter), lots of vegetables, and a high-quality, high-fiber complex carbohydrate (whole-wheat spaghetti).

Excellent. Added sugar is genuinely zero (the natural peanut butter is specified as having no added sugar), and there is a robust, quality carbohydrate component (48.7g total carbs) that fits the nutrient tier window perfectly to prevent hypoglycemia.
Fits the 'Lunches' chapter flawlessly. It hits all nutrient targets (protein ≥ 26g, fiber ≥ 7g, carbs 32-55g), is batch-friendly, and is designed to be eaten cold.

Even factoring in the time required to bring water to a boil from a cold start, prep (mincing garlic, whisking dressing, slicing cucumber) can easily be done concurrently. The whole dish comfortably finishes under 25 minutes using ubiquitous supermarket ingredients.
